name: The Kappa
description: A polite but dangerous river imp with a dish of water on its head

debut.title: Japanese yōkai tales
debut.era: widely recorded in the Edo period (1603–1868)

legend: Kappa are yōkai that lurk in Japan's rivers and ponds. They're about the size of a child, with a beak, a shell and a dish-shaped hollow on top of the head that holds water, the source of their strength. Kappa drag people and horses into the water and love to challenge passers-by to sumo. But they're bound by manners: bow to a kappa and it must bow back, spilling its water. And a kappa that makes a promise always keeps it.

myths.claim: Bowing to a kappa can save your life.
myths.explanation: It is so polite that it bows back, spills the water from its head and loses its strength.

myths.claim: Kappa-maki sushi is named after the creature.
myths.explanation: Cucumber rolls are named after the kappa's favourite food.
Some tales have grateful kappa helping farmers or teaching people how to set broken bones.

weaknesses: Spilling the water on its head
legacy: A mascot for towns, sushi and water-safety campaigns across Japan
facts: The kappa carries a dish of water in the top of its head
If that water spills, the kappa loses its strength
It is so polite that it must bow back if you bow to it
Its favourite food is cucumber, which gave kappa-maki its name
Kappa love to challenge people to sumo wrestling
A kappa that makes a promise always keeps it
hostIntro: Tonight's guest lives at the bottom of the river and loves a wrestling match. Remember your manners, and bring cucumbers.
